characters.continuity: DC Comics mainstream (Post-Crisis New Earth through New 52 / Prime Earth); era noted per entry
characters.summary: Darkseid is the ruler of Apokolips, an immortal New God with superhuman strength, speed and a heated cosmic beam (the Omega Effect) that can disintegrate targets or erase them from existence.

techniques: Omega Beams (can curve around corners, disintegrate, or cause a target never to have existed)
Teleportation of himself or others through time and space; Boom Tubes

mechanisms: Nigh-immortal New God physiology (but has been killed on several occasions)
Prime Earth: unfazed by the combined assault of the Justice League (Justice League vol. 2 #6)

weaknesses: Radion: in Final Crisis Batman shot him with the radion bullet that had killed Orion
limitations: Prefers to use his intelligence to manipulate or control others rather than fight personally

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: Green Lantern ring feat, overpowering two Kryptonians and the Justice League, Omega Beams (curve, disintegrate, erase from existence), teleporting self or others through time and space, telepathy, telekinesis, size increase, killed on several occasions, prefers manipulation; Final Crisis deaths (Orion, radion bullet, Superman). Re-read 2026-11-13 via a March 2026 Kiwix copy of the article: https://wiki.krisyotam.com/content/wikipedia_en_all_nopic_2026-03/Darkseid

Prime Earth powers: strength rivals a Kryptonian's, unfazed by the Justice League's combined assault (Justice League vol. 2 #6), telepathy, telekinesis, size adjustment, Boom Tube travel; defeated and captured Superman during the war on Earth; killed Zeus and absorbed his power.

feats.claim: Effortlessly broke a Green Lantern ring with his bare hands; easily overpowered two Kryptonians at once and defeated the entire Justice League.
feats.citation: Wikipedia: Darkseid, Powers and abilities (no issue named)

feats.claim: Prime Earth: remained unfazed by the combined assault of the Justice League.
feats.citation: Justice League vol. 2 #6, per DC Database

feats.claim: Prime Earth: killed Zeus, absorbed his power and restored his own.

notableResults.citation: DC Database: Darkseid (Prime Earth), History (New 52 war on Earth)
notableResults.note: Overpowered Superman's allies, defeated and captured Superman; Batman later freed him and Superman pushed Darkseid back through a Boom Tube.
Orion killed Darkseid by ripping his heart out.
Superman destroyed him with counter-vibrations at the end of Final Crisis.

campaignTags.claim: Can teleport himself through time and space.
Can teleport others through time and space.

unknowns: Removed in earlier review: flight, healing factor, energy-projection resistance, "The Source" as a weakness, mirror-deflected Omega Beams.

Corrected 2026-11-13: the earlier list of characters who "defeated" him (Quintessence, Black Racer, Eclipso, Doomsday) is not in the article; it says only that Doomsday can resist the Omega Beams. Radion as a general New God toxin is not stated by either source; only the Final Crisis radion bullet is.
The Green Lantern ring and two-Kryptonian feats name no issue; continuity era unconfirmed.
Durability is not quantified; limits vary across eras.

characters.summary: In Infinite Frontier, Darkseid is trapped on Earth-Omega, regains his original form by fusing with his alternate-universe counterparts, battles the Justice League Incarnate and is defeated by the Great Hand.

techniques: Omega Beams (inherited from base Darkseid; no variant-specific evidence)

mechanisms: Base Darkseid physiology (inherited); no variant-specific durability is sourced

weaknesses: Was controlled by Pariah and the Great Darkness after his defeat, until freed by Nightwing
characters.formDifferences: Regained his original form by fusing with alternate-universe counterparts on Earth-Omega. The source gives no evidence of enhanced multiversal durability, reality warping or conceptual immunity.

sources.supports: Infinite Frontier section: Earth-Omega, fusion with counterparts, Justice League Incarnate fight, defeat by the Great Hand, control by Pariah and the Great Darkness.

Infinite Frontier history: imprisoned on Earth-Omega by the Quintessence, fused with prior incarnations and alternate selves and broke free; fought the Gentry's leader the Empty Hand and was defeated; the Great Darkness then took control of his mind (Justice League Incarnate, 2021-22).

notableResults.citation: Justice League Incarnate (2021-22), per DC Database; Wikipedia: Darkseid, Infinite Frontier
notableResults.note: Defeated and sent to a void where the Great Darkness (with Pariah) controlled him; Nightwing later freed him (Wikipedia). Wikipedia names the victor "the Great Hand"; DC Database names the Empty Hand.

conditional.dependsOn: Fusing with his alternate-universe counterparts on Earth-Omega

unknowns: Removed unsupported "multiversal durability", "conceptual immunity", "reality warping", "Empty Hand" absorption and flight; none appear in the source.
Powers are inherited from the base form with no variant-specific evidence; owner should confirm scaling.
Opponent name conflict: Wikipedia says "Great Hand", DC Database says the Empty Hand, the Gentry's leader. Recorded as the Empty Hand; confirm against Justice League Incarnate #4-5.

characters.summary: Deadshot has no superhuman powers but is the top marksman in the DC Universe, with superhuman-like accuracy, wrist-mounted guns, a sniper rifle and a mask lens over his right eye that aids his aim.

mechanisms: No superhuman durability; relies on marksmanship and equipment

limitations: Entirely dependent on conventional weapons and skill

sources.supports: No superhuman powers, top marksman in the DC Universe with superhuman-like accuracy, "never misses" boast, twin wrist-mounted guns, sniper rifle, mask lens over right eye aiding aim, firearms expert. Re-read 2026-11-13 via Wikiwand.

feats.claim: Described as the top marksman in the DC Universe with superhuman-like accuracy.

campaignTags.claim: Twin wrist-mounted guns and a mask with a multi-use lens over his right eye that aids his aim.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: a mile-long shot in Suicide Squad #1, tactical body armor, vehicle mobility, a loss to Batman with no issue sourced, and a melee-vulnerability weakness.
Corrected 2026-11-13: the article describes a multi-use lens, not a telescopic sight, and says "expert in firearms", not expertise with all firearms and projectile weapons.

characters.summary: Death of the Endless is the personification of the end of life, described as an immortal being of virtual omnipotence, omniscience and omnipresence who can prevent aging and death if she chooses.

techniques: Ending life as the personification of Death
Preventing or granting aging and death at will

mechanisms: Immortal; Death itself rather than an agent of death

weaknesses: Not established; no combat vulnerability is sourced
limitations: Must live out the last day of a random mortal one day each century

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: virtual omnipotence, immortality, ability to prevent aging and death; the one-day-per-century mortal limitation.

feats.claim: Prevented a man from aging and dying by granting his wish never to die.
feats.citation: Wikipedia: Death of the Endless, Powers and abilities

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: invulnerability to physical force, reality manipulation, self-teleportation, a cosmic-charter weakness and a "last entity alive" feat (a stated role, not a feat).
Conceptual, near-omnipotent character: combat modelling is outcome-critical and needs manual research and an owner ruling.

characters.summary: Deathstroke (Slade Wilson) is an elite mercenary whose super-soldier serum gives enhanced strength, speed, durability and a healing factor; he is a master of martial arts, swords and firearms.

techniques: Swords, knives and a ballistic staff firing energy bolts

mechanisms: Healing factor (recovered from impalement and brain bullet wounds)

weaknesses: Blind in his right eye (a bullet penetrated it in his origin)
limitations: Healing factor is stated to cover only non-fatal injuries, though he has healed severe trauma
Superhuman but not invulnerable; no powers beyond his enhancements and weapons

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: serum-granted enhancements, healing factor, toxin resistance, combat training and weapons. Origin: a bullet penetrated his right eye, blinding it.

feats.claim: Healed from severe organ trauma including impalement and bullet wounds to the brain.

campaignTags.claim: Healing factor recovers from severe injuries including brain wounds.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: Nth metal armor, a Teen Titans win in New Teen Titans #2, an inconclusive result vs Batman, and a "gadgets" tag (his equipment is weapons).

characters.continuity: DC Comics New 52, Deathstroke vol. 3 (2014-16), "Godkiller" arc (#7-11)
characters.summary: Godkiller Deathstroke is Slade Wilson in the New 52 "Godkiller" arc, armed by Hephaestus with a god-killing sword commissioned by Apollo, which he used to kill the Titan Iapetus.

techniques: Base Deathstroke martial arts, swords and firearms (inherited)

mechanisms: Serum-enhanced durability and healing factor (inherited from base Deathstroke)

characters.formDifferences: Adds a god-killing sword forged by Hephaestus at Apollo's request. Godkiller armor and any change in durability are not described by the sources opened.

sources.supports: Base Deathstroke powers and weapons; the page names the collected edition "Deathstroke Vol. 2: God Killer" but does not describe the form.
Official solicitation: armed by Hephaestus with a new weapon capable of taking down an Olympian god.
Review of Deathstroke #10 (2015): Deathstroke uses the god-killing sword Apollo had Hephaestus make and kills the Titan Iapetus.

notableResults.note: Killed the Titan with the god-killing sword; the review spells the name "Lapetus". Apollo had engineered the job as a con.

unknowns: Corrected 2026-11-13: continuity was "Darkseid War"; the Godkiller story is the Deathstroke vol. 3 (2014) arc. The sword is now sourced to the DC solicitation and an issue review.
Godkiller armor and any durability change remain unsourced; durability and healing are inherited from base Deathstroke.
Kept needs-review: variant-specific scaling beyond the sword still needs manual research.
Unsupported by cited source (term check, 3/8 key terms found): Ability to kill gods depends on Wielding the god-killing sword forged by Hephaestus

characters.continuity: DC Comics, Kent Nelson incarnation (Golden Age through Modern Era)
characters.summary: Doctor Fate is a sorcerer empowered by the Lords of Order through the Helmet of Fate, Amulet of Anubis and Cloak of Destiny, with flight, teleportation, precognition and illusion casting.

techniques: Sorcery of the Lords of Order
Precognition via the Helmet of Fate

mechanisms: Amulet of Anubis: resistance to psychic and astral probing and mind control; contains a separate universe able to trap entities
Cloak of Destiny: invulnerability, fireproof, counters magic of the Lords of Chaos
Invulnerability: withstood military weapons and a mansion-destroying explosion (DC Database)

weaknesses: Inferior in power to the Spectre and cannot cast counter spells against him, due to the "rules of magic"
Without the Helm of Fate he is significantly weakened (Doctor Fate vol. 2 #36)
limitations: Power level described as inconsistent across stories
Older incarnations diminish in power over time

sources.supports: Powers, weaknesses and reception: artifacts and their protections, flight, teleportation, precognition, illusions, Spectre inferiority and counter-spell rule, older hosts diminishing, inconsistent power level, among the most powerful magical practitioners. Re-read 2026-11-13 via a March 2026 Kiwix copy: https://wiki.krisyotam.com/content/wikipedia_en_all_nopic_2026-03/Dr._Fate

Kent Nelson (New Earth): invulnerability feats, teleportation, weakened without the Helm (Doctor Fate vol. 2 #36), defeat by the Spectre under Kulak's control (All-Star Squadron #23), win over Wotan (More Fun Comics #56).

feats.claim: Withstood military weapons and an explosion able to destroy a mansion.
feats.citation: DC Database: Kent Nelson (New Earth), Equipment

notableResults.note: Defeated by the Spectre while Kulak controlled him.

notableResults.citation: More Fun Comics #56, per DC Database
notableResults.note: Defeated Wotan and locked him away.

conditional.ability: Full Lord of Order magical mastery
conditional.dependsOn: Wearing the Helm of Fate; without it he is significantly weakened

campaignTags.claim: Described as a sorcerous hero and one of the most powerful magic wielders.
Flight via mystical artifacts such as the Cloak of Destiny.
Draws his power from the Helmet of Fate, Amulet of Anubis and Cloak of Destiny.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: a Justice League of America #1 feat, an inconclusive Day of Judgment result, a loss of power when separated from the helmet, and an "Amulet shield" mechanism.
Several incarnations (Nelson, Strauss, Hall, Nassour) differ; the record follows the page generally and is not incarnation-specific.

Corrected 2026-11-13: the earlier defense "cannot be countered by counter spells" inverted the source. The article says Fate cannot cast counter spells against the Spectre; moved to weaknesses. The Spectre "loss" was a power comparison; replaced with a real fight from DC Database.

characters.summary: Doctor Manhattan is a Watchmen-born being with complete control over atomic and subatomic matter, able to teleport, fly, phase, disintegrate people, rebuild his body and perceive past, present and future at once.

mechanisms: Reconstructs his body within seconds after disintegration

limitations: Uses levitation more often than full flight
Could not erase or permanently kill Eobard Thawne despite his power

sources.supports: Powers and abilities: atomic control, teleportation, flight, phasing, force fields, disintegration, time perception, DC Universe timeline alteration and the Thawne limit. Re-read 2026-11-13 via Wikiwand.

feats.claim: Instantaneously disintegrated fleeing soldiers during the Vietnam War with a thought.
feats.citation: Wikipedia: Doctor Manhattan, Powers and abilities

feats.claim: Erased ten years from the DC Universe through time manipulation, leading to the New 52 timeline.
feats.citation: Wikipedia: Doctor Manhattan, Powers and abilities

campaignTags.claim: Capable of true flight though he mostly levitates.
Can teleport himself over limitless distances.
Can teleport others over limitless distances.
Can move objects without touching them.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: a Watchmen #4 citation for the disintegration feat, a tachyon-field weakness, "quantum regeneration" as worded, and an inconclusive Superman result.
Extreme, outcome-changing reality-warping scaling; continuity-specific treatment needs an owner ruling before use in the engine.

characters.summary: Dream of the Endless is the ruler of the Dreaming, one of the seven Endless, inconceivably powerful beings; the cited page gives little combat detail and records his death at the hands of the Furies in The Kindly Ones.

techniques: Rule over the Dreaming, a realm mutable at his will

limitations: His realm and he himself resist change; narrative note only

sources.supports: Character overview: ruler of the Dreaming, one of the Endless, death at the hands of the Furies, succession by Daniel.

notableResults.citation: The Sandman, "The Kindly Ones", per Wikipedia
notableResults.note: Killed by the Furies; Daniel Hall became the new Dream.

unknowns: Removed unsupported claims: conceptual immortality, dream-realm regeneration, trapping mortals and immortals in slumber, an inconclusive result vs Lucifer, and a totems-of-office weakness. The page does not mention them.
Combat abilities need manual research from The Sandman before any scaling.
